Anita Zhu
Director of Investor Relations, Daqo New Energy
Hello, everyone. I'm Anita, the investor relations of Daqo New Energy. Thank you for joining our conference call today. Daqo New Energy just issued its financial results for Q1 2024, which can be found on our website at www.dqsolar.com. Today, attending our conference call, we have our chairman and CEO, Mr. Xiang Xu, our CFO, Mr. Ming Yang, and myself. The call today will begin with an update from Mr. Xu on market conditions and company operations, and then Mr. Yang will discuss the company's financial performance for the quarter. After that, we will open the floor to Q&A from the audience. Before we begin the formal remarks,
I would like to remind you that certain statements on today's call, including expected future operational and financial performance and industry growth, are forward-looking statements that are made under the Safe Harbor provisions of the US Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements involve inherent risks and uncertainties. A number of factors could cause actual results to differ materially from those contained in any forward-looking statements. Further information regarding these and other risks is included in the reports or documents we have filed with or furnished to the Securities and Exchange Commission.
These statements only reflect our current and preliminary view as of today, and may be subject to change. Our ability to achieve these projections is subject to risks and uncertainties. All information provided in today's call is as of today, and we undertake no duty to update such information except as required under applicable law. Also, during the call, we'll occasionally reference monetary amounts in US dollar terms. Please keep in mind that our functional currency is the Chinese RMB. We offer these translations into US dollars solely for the convenience of the audience.
Mr. Xu will make his remarks regarding current market conditions and company performance in Chinese, which I will translate into English after he finishes. Now I'll turn the call to our CEO. [Foreign language]
Xiang Xu
Chairman and CEO, Daqo New Energy
Thank you, Anita. [Foreign language]
Anita Zhu
Director of Investor Relations, Daqo New Energy
Hello everyone, this is Anita. Thank you for joining the call. I'll now translate our CEO Mr. Xiang Xu's remarks. During Q1, we continued to optimize our manufacturing operations, and made improvements in both yields and throughput at our two poly facilities. Total production volume for the quarter was 62,278 metric tons, which was above our expectations and represented an increase of 1,264 metric tons compared to the previous quarter. Our Inner Mongolia 5A facility contributed 46% of our total production volume for Q1. Through achievements in R&D and significant purity improvements at both facilities, we've further increased our N-type product mix from 60% in December last year to 72% in March.
Compared to the end of last year, production costs trended down over the quarter, decreasing further by 2% from Q4 2023 to an average of $6.737 per kg in Q1 2024. For the quarter, we generated $77 million in EBITDA. By the end of Q1 2024, the company maintained a strong cash balance of $2.7 billion and a combined cash and bank note receivable balance of $2.9 billion. We expect Q2 2024 total poly production volume to be approximately 60,000 metric tons to 63,000 metric tons, similar to that of Q1 2024 as the company maintains full production.
We expect to finish construction and begin initial pilot production at our new Inner Mongolia Phase 5B facility in Q2 2024, and expect to ramp up to full production level by the end of Q3 2024. As a result, we anticipate full year 2024 production volume to be in the range of 280,000 to 300,000 metric tons, approximately 40% to 50% higher than that of 2023. With more than 15 years of experience in poly production, as well as a fully digitalized and integrated production system that optimizes operational efficiency, we'll continue to increase our N-type production in the product mix. During Q1, the solar market initially showed signs of strength as we head into the Chinese New Year holiday in February.
Despite the production cuts and downtime as usual during the holidays, polysilicon demand had been strong pre-holiday as wafer manufacturers kept utilization rates unchanged or even higher in anticipation of higher demand, and better product pricing post holidays. The general polysilicon price range was CNY 65 to 70 per kg for N-type, and CNY 55 to 60 per kg for P-type during this period. However, with weaker than expected production plans downstream starting March, the wafer sector faced significant pressure from accumulated inventories and negative margins. Market sentiment shifted significantly in mid-March, with widespread expectations of falling prices throughout the value chain, particularly for polysilicon. As a result, downstream manufacturers began to lower utilization, reduce inventory, and delay orders to minimize the impact of falling prices.
In April, further pressure on polysilicon prices emerged as the issue of excess inventory among wafer manufacturers worsened, and wafer customers further delayed orders, and product delivery. Therefore, polysilicon prices dropped further by late April to CNY 47 to 54 per kg for tier one producers at the industry's cash break-even cost. At this level, we believe the entire solar value chain, including polysilicon, is likely to be loss-making in general, and that a large number of polysilicon producers are currently unprofitable. The solar industry has gone through multiple cycles in the past, and based on our previous experience, we believe that the current low prices and market downturn will eventually result in a healthier market as poor profitability and losses, as well as cash burn, will lead to many market players exiting the business with some possible bankruptcies.
This will bring the inevitable capacity rationalization, and solve the overcapacity issue we're currently experiencing. As demand growth resumes after excess inventories are depleted in the short term, and on the backdrop of positive policies pushing renewable installations in the long run, the solar PV industry will return to normal profitability, and achieve better margins. We believe that at the end of the quarter, we had one of the industry's lowest levels of finished goods inventory, with approximately two weeks of production. Overall, 2023 marked a step change for renewable power growth, with China's newly installed solar PV capacity reaching a record high of 216.9GW, representing 148% year-over-year growth.
We continue to see strong growth in solar PV installations in China during Q1 2024, which reached an aggregate of 45.7GW, representing a 36% year-over-year growth rate. Solar has become one of the most competitive forms of power generation, and continuous cost reductions in solar PV products and associated reductions in solar energy generation costs are expected to create substantial additional demand for solar PV. With 2023 setting the stage for gradually phasing out P-type products, we believe that 2024 will mark the year when N-type products dominate the industry. We are optimistic that we'll capture the long-term benefits of the growing global solar PV market and maintain our competitive advantage by enhancing our higher efficiency N-type technology and optimizing our cost structure through digital transformation, and AI adoption.
As one of the world's lowest cost producers with the highest quality N-type product, a strong balance sheet, and no financial debt, we believe we're very well positioned to weather the current market down cycle and emerge as one of the leaders in the industry to capture the market's future growth. Now I'll turn the call to our CFO, Mr. Ming Yang, who will discuss the company's financial performance for the quarter. Ming, please go ahead.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Hello, everyone. This is Ming Yang, CFO of Daqo New Energy. We appreciate you joining our earnings conference call today. I will now go over the company's Q1 2024 financial performance. Revenues were CNY 415.3 million, compared to CNY 476.3 million in the Q4 of 2023 and CNY 709 million in the Q1 of 2023. The decrease in revenue compared to the Q4 of 2023 was primarily due to a decrease in average selling prices, and lower polysilicon sales volume. Gross profit was CNY 72 million, compared to CNY 87 million in the Q4 of 2023 and CNY 506 million in the Q1 of 2023.
Gross margin was 17.4%, compared to 18.3% in Q4 2023 and 71.4% in Q1 2023. The decrease in gross margin compared to Q4 2023 was primarily due to lower average selling prices, which was partially mitigated by lower production costs. Selling, general, and administrative expenses were CNY 38.4 million, compared to CNY 39 million in Q4 2023 and CNY 41.3 million in Q1 2023. SG&A expenses during the first quarter included CNY 19.6 million in non-cash share-based compensation costs related to the company's share incentive plan, compared to CNY 19.6 million in Q4 2023.
R&D expenses were CNY 1.5 million, compared to CNY 3.3 million in Q4 2023 and CNY 1.9 million in Q1 2023. R&D expenses vary from period to period, and reflect the R&D activities that take place during the quarter. Our R&D activities currently focus on process and technologies that improve purity for the polysilicon, and re-remove contamination to increase our N-type polysilicon percentage. As a result of the foregoing, income from operations were CNY 30.5 million, compared to CNY 83.3 million in Q4 2023 and CNY 463.8 million in Q1 2023. Operating margin was 7.3%, compared to 17.5% in Q4 2023 and 65% in Q1 2023.
Foreign exchange loss was CNY 0.3 million, compared to a loss of CNY 0.8 million in Q4 2023, and this is attributed to the volatility and fluctuation of the US dollar to our RMB exchange rate during the quarter. Net income attributable to Daqo New Energy shareholders was CNY 15.5 million, compared to CNY 53.3 million in Q4 2023 and CNY 278.8 million in Q1 2023. Earnings per basic ADS was $0.24, compared to $0.76 in Q4 2023 and $3.56 in Q1 2023.
Adjusted net income attributable to Daqo New Energy Corp. shareholders, excluding non-cash share-based compensation costs, was $36 million, compared to $74.3 million in Q4 of 2023 and $310 million in Q1 of 2023. Adjusted earnings per basic ADS was $0.55, compared to $1.06 in Q4 of 2023 and $3.96 in Q1 of 2023. EBITDA was $76.9 million, compared to $128 million in Q4 of 2023 and $490 million in Q1 of 2023. EBITDA margin was 18.5%, compared to 26.9% in Q4 of 2023 and 69% in Q1 of 2023. Now the company's financial condition.
As of 31 March 2024, the company had CNY 2.689 billion in cash and cash equivalents, compared to CNY 3.05 billion as of 31 December 2023, and CNY 4.1 billion as of 31 March 2023. As of 31 March 2024, the notes receivable balance was CNY 194 million, compared to CNY 116 million as of 31 December 2023, and CNY 791 million as of 31 March 2023. No receivables represent bank notes with maturity within six months. For the three months ended 31 March 2024, net cash used in operating activities was CNY 115.9 million, compared to net cash provided by operating activities of CNY 807 million in the same period of 2023.
Net cash used in operating activities for the quarter was a result of change in operating assets and liabilities, primarily related to the company's payment of approximately $75 million in tax payables that is due during Q1, as well as an increase in notes receivable balance of approximately $78 million. Other items that used cash include payments to suppliers in conjunction with the period related to the Chinese New Year holidays, as well as the increase in inventory. For the three months ended 31 March 2024, net cash used in investing activities was $190.5 million, compared to $268.9 million in the same period of 2023.
Net cash used in investing activities in Q1 2024 was primarily related to the capital expenditures on the company's Phase 5A and Phase 5B polysilicon expansion projects in Baotou City, Inner Mongolia. Due to the recent changes in market condition, the company's board and management team have decided to temporarily postpone the company's non-polysilicon manufacturing capacity expansion plans to reserve capital. As such, the company's capital expenditure plan has been reduced to approximately $700 million for the year, which is related to the company's Inner Mongolia polysilicon project. This represents a significant decrease from the previous capital expenditure plan for the year of approximately $1.1 to 1.2 billion.
For the three months ended 31 March 2024, net cash used in finance activity was CNY 6 million, compared to net cash provided by finance activities of CNY 59.9 million in the same period of 2023. Net cash used in finance activity in Q1 2024 was primarily related to approximately $5 million that we used for the company's share repurchase. That concludes our prepared remarks. We will now open the call to Q&A from the audience. Operator, please begin.
Operator
We will now begin the question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you may press star, then one on your touchtone phone. If you are using a speakerphone, please pick up your handset before pressing the keys. If at any time your question has been addressed and you would like to withdraw your question, please press star, then two. At this time, we will pause momentarily to assemble our roster. The first question today comes from Phil Shen with Roth MKM. Please go ahead. Phil, your line is open if you'd like to ask your question. We seem to be unable to connect to Phil Shen's audio. The next question comes from Alan Lau with Jefferies. Please go ahead.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Thanks a lot for taking my question, management. I think the first question that I've received after the announcement is about the buyback. I wonder if there's any guidance from the management in regards to buyback or dividends planned in this year.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Okay. The board actually had a discussion about potentially continuing to do the share repurchase program. I think in light of the current market condition, where you know the industry overall is actually looking like it's going to be making losses, and we're uncertain how long this might last. The board does feel that it's more prudent to conserve capital for now to weather the market downturn. They would like to see, you know, how the market would perform. If the market does improve perhaps later in the year, I think the board would definitely consider a program at a later date as appropriate.
I think just, you know, because of the market condition, I think the board does feel that we need to conserve capital, including that we significantly reduced our capacity expansion plans. Separately, I think the company is also strategically looking at potential expansions overseas outside of China, you know, including in areas in Middle East, where we're actually looking at several locations pretty actively, and then also potentially in other areas in Southeast Asia as well. That also represents a potential use of funds for the company. The board is also making some considerations because of that as well.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
I see. Yeah. Another question I have is on the sales volume. In terms of the production, actually the company has an upside surprise in the production volume, but the sales seems lower than the production volume. We'd like to know how much is the inventory right now in the company, and also in regards to the sales volume in Q1, was it related to the cut in utilization rate in wafer segment?
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Okay. Yes. I think operationally the company actually was doing very well. This quarter, I think if you exclude the impact of the market condition the H2 of March, I think, you know, we produced more than 62,000 metric tons, right, increase over the previous quarter. This is a pretty good improvement. Particularly on the quality side, we made very significant improvements in quality, particularly in the Mongolia facility. N-type as of March is now north of 70% of our mix. And at the same time, we also saw further reduction in production costs. I think just such that, you know, since mid-March, the industry conditions declined significantly. I think customers delayed their orders.
They delayed delivery of polysilicon for production. They lowered the utilization, I think, in anticipation of lower polysilicon pricing, but also because of the significant wafer inventory that was occurring at the time. Yeah. Actually, this situation actually persisted more or less through mid to late April. I think now we're shipping normally, but at a much lower pricing. At the end of the quarter, we had approximately two weeks, slightly less than two weeks, of production of finished goods inventory. We think that's probably one of the lowest within the industry.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Yeah. Two weeks of inventory is actually quite impressive. Another question I have is on the other operating income. The QoQ change is relatively significant. I'd like to know, is it related to the change in the subsidies provided in terms of the power tariff?
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Actually I believe we had other. It's actually an expense for the quarter rather than an income, and then it's related to some of the older equipment that we've replaced. The old equipment needs to be expensed. It's no longer being used. Its amount is about $1.6 million, so it's not too significant. This happens, you know, like maybe once a year or something like that.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
I see. I understand. In the Q1, there isn't any subsidies coming in, right? Like in Q4.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Yeah. We would expect some subsidy potentially in Q2 and then, you know, more subsidy likely in Q4. Well, usually it's in H2 of the year.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
I see. I think my last question is in regards to the industry, like, how do you see the poly price going forward this year? And then, when do you see a turnaround in the industry?
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Okay. The most recent price decline we believe actually is more of a result than the inventory adjustment that's happening, right? Customers delaying orders and with the expectations of a lower pricing in future periods, right? Some people then wanna take a wait and see mode. Now at the lower price, we're starting to see orders returning also at a lower level, lower pricing level. We think the pricing level where the industry is at right now is actually money losing probably for, I would call 70%, 80% of the industry. I think almost majority of the players are losing money right now, and this certainly cannot be sustainable.
I think if this price drop persists, it's a matter of time that a number of players will likely need to shut down or some may even, you know, exit the business or go into bankruptcy. I think we're likely to see that if price stays at this low level. Then that will bring the eventual capacity rationalization, right? I think that people are expecting. At the same time, you also have a lot of opportunity on demand. We think China is likely to be very strong this year because of where the panel price is right now. It's offering very high return for the solar projects here in China. I think globally as well.
We are optimistic that we could see a very significant end market this year. I think it's the balance of these two. I think timing is hard to tell. I think we could see some improvements in H2 of this year.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
I see. Another thing is, a lot of players are actually losing money. Are you going to delay your Phase 5B or like, what is the cap that is going to look like this year, especially at current prices?
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
We're delaying everything else, almost everything else except 5B. 'Cause 5B is already ready to go into production, like, 'cause it's been under construction for a year or over a year. I think 5B we're still at least for now, as of today, it's still you know being planned as originally scheduled you know to start production in Q2, in this quarter, actually. Initial production and then you know ramp up in Q3.
Alan Lau
Managing Director and Senior Equity Research Analyst, Jefferies
Thanks. I'll pass on to other investors. Thanks a lot for taking my questions.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Okay. Thank you.
Operator
The next question comes from Leo Ho with Daiwa Capital Markets. Please go ahead.
Leo Ho
VP of Equity Research, Daiwa Capital Markets
Thanks, management, for the time today. My first question is regarding the FBR granular silicon. We noticed that there are several major module makers including, for example, LONGi and JinkoSolar, suggesting that the FBR doping ratio now they can do around 50% for N-type wafer. I just wonder if we can share any update on, you know, this FBR usage situation, what's our take, and then, you know, why we're seeing such a sudden increase in the doping ratio. Thank you.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
I think on the FBR, at least based on feedback from our customers, that it continues to have, you know, higher levels of contaminants, and a higher surface metal and a higher hydrogen and higher carbon. I think the challenge with most of the wafer producer is that the higher carbon content actually leads to breaking of the crucible. And then also, the contamination and also the hydrogen jumping issue means that less amount of poly can be used per run. If you use FBR, you have a slight reduction in production yield per run on the ingot. And that's the main reason why customers require a discount and currently primarily use it as a mix.
In the previous understanding is, the mix is between 10% to 30%. You know, I think every producer probably has a slightly different mix. I think, you know, some of the main players. All these players are also our customer, right? I think either they wanna diversify their sourcing or maybe they wanna lower their costs, right? They're, I mean, they're always looking for lower cost sources to the extent that they can use, right? We're not surprised that they are near some kind of agreement. These agreements are always, at least in China, almost always, these are kind of framework agreements, right? The volume and pricing is adjusted on a monthly basis.
Leo Ho
VP of Equity Research, Daiwa Capital Markets
Understood. That's clear. My next question is regarding the price gap for different type of polysilicon, say for example, n-type versus p-type, and then also for n-type high-quality polysilicon that we produce against FBR. What are those, like, price gaps going to look like right now and also looking forward? Thank you.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
I think consistently the N-type poly has had price premium in the range of maybe CNY 5 to 10 per kg. I think currently it's somewhere in the CNY 7 to 8 per kg still, you know, even at the current pricing. While FBR is generally priced at a discount to the P-type poly, generally. Obviously FBR has different grades, right? Yeah. Within N-type and P-type, there is also different grades, you know, generally, related to the form factor of the surface structure. It's not like one single price. It's usually a range of price.
Leo Ho
VP of Equity Research, Daiwa Capital Markets
My last question is regarding electricity tariff for our Baotou and Shihezi capacities. Would there be any, like, electricity tariff changes that we expected for this year or for next year?
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Are we expecting any electricity tariff adjustments on the electricity rates?
Leo Ho
VP of Equity Research, Daiwa Capital Markets
Thanks so much.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Thank you.
Leo Ho
VP of Equity Research, Daiwa Capital Markets
That's very clear. Thank you.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Okay. I think for Xinjiang, we're expecting the rate to be very stable. I think the rate has been fixed. The previous adjustments was mostly related to, I think a policy issued by NDRC that kind of forbid, you know, single entity type of energy price structure. At the same time, it also coincided a time where the coal prices was at a higher price. Our utility company actually was losing money on the power sales to us on the power they generate. After the rate adjustment, that's no longer the case. I mean, we continue to have the most favorable utility rate, you know, for that local utility or for the region.
Very still competitive. We don't expect that to change, or the rate to change. I think similarly for Inner Mongolia. Inner Mongolia already had an adjustment, I think around in the H1 of 2023, I believe, also based on the NDRC rule. Now the Inner Mongolia rate structure is actually a market-based structure where actually the rate is not fixed. It's actually floating based on market supply and demand for the utility market. Because we buy a significant portion of our power comes from renewables, and renewable pricing utility is lower than coal for the Inner Mongolia grid. Also we have the most preferential pricing for the whole local grid there.
We think we have a very competitive utility price there, and we don't expect that to change. It's already been adjusted.
Leo Ho
VP of Equity Research, Daiwa Capital Markets
Thank you so much for the additional color. These are all from my side, I think it's.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Oh, great. Thank you.
Operator
As a reminder, if you would like to ask a question, please press star then one to enter the question queue. The next question comes from Phil Shen with Roth MKM. Please go ahead.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Hi, everyone. Thanks for taking my questions. Sorry about the technical difficulties earlier. I'd like to explore price just a little bit more. Can you give us a sense of pricing beyond this year as well? Do you think there could be some recovery next year? We've seen price decline recently, and some of the experts that we've been consulting with suggest that, you know, prices will continue to decline as we go through the year. Wondering if you can give us a view of 2025. Thanks.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Okay. We do think pricing is probably at the bottom, or if not at the bottom, near the very bottom. It's already below cash break-even price for a lot of the producers. We think 70% to 80%. We think starting in the next two months or so, we will start to see shutdown. We're already starting to see shutdowns. We will see more shutdowns going forward. If this, say, persists through Q3, then we think some of the producers will run into cash problem. If it goes into next year, I mean, we might see an OCI-like type of shutdown, right? I think, I don't know, some of the investors might remember OCI shutdown in 2020. I think that was. They kind of gave up.
I think if price stays low, we will see this kind of condition. We don't think price can stay this low until, say, through next year. Certainly, you will have much lower production of poly than, you know, poly is not sufficient to service the market and demand grows, right? Because and then some of it, the current market condition is due to inventory adjustments, right? I mean, ultimately, the downstream customers will need to restart buying again, right? Because they bought probably more than they need in, say, in the H1 of the quarter. Then when, you know, their expected demand or price increase did not materialize in H2f of March, that's when they slowed down or stopped ordering.
It's kind of the market behavior that's creating kind of the volatility that we're seeing in the market right now.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Got it. Thanks, Ming. Can you talk about the amount of channel inventory that's in the market now? Do you expect that to continue to grow for the near term? When do you think that peaks? Thanks.

CFO, Daqo New Energy
We've heard it's somewhere in the range of 150 to 180 thousand metric tons right now of channel inventory. We're a very insignificant part of that. Some of our peers, our main peers, actually have a lot of inventory currently. We'll see how that works.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Okay. Then you talked about 70% to 80% are losing money. What's your guess as to what percentage of the industry could be shut down by the end of the year? I mean, do you think it could be as much as a quarter of the industry could be, you know, shut down? What percentage of the industry could go out of business and maybe-
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Sure.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
What are your thoughts on that? Thanks.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
This is very ballpark. I think about half would shut down.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Okay. Half can exit the industry.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Yeah. Yeah. I mean, yeah. I think capacity that's kind of in Sichuan is definitely not competitive. The capacity in Yining is not competitive at the current market. Some, even some capacity in Inner Mongolia is competitive at the current price.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Okay, last question.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
cannot produce sustainably, yeah. Okay.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Yeah. Oh, thank you. What are your thoughts on the Chinese government stepping in to influence or regulate, you know, maybe setting price caps or something like that? We were reading and seeing some potential for that for the module industry. Do you think there could be something like that for poly where the government steps in to avoid this overcapacity in the future?
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
We haven't heard about that at all. No, we haven't seen any government actions related to that.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
Okay. Thank you very much.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
No.
Philip Shen
Managing Director and Senior Research Analyst, ROTH MKM
I'll pass that on.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Okay. Thank you.

Alan Hon
Executive Director of Equity Research, JPMorgan
Hi, this is Alan from JP Morgan. I have like questions on the amount of capacity in the system right now and also like the outlook in the next one to two quarters. I mean, other than you, who else would be adding capacity? That would be my first questions.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Our understanding is capacity in the system is around maybe 1.8 to 2 million tons per year.
Alan Hon
Executive Director of Equity Research, JPMorgan
Got it. My second question is like, what do you expect your cost structure will be with the new plant commencement in Q2? Or for the new plant, what do you expect the new plant's cost structure will be?
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Okay. I think at least as of today, so we are expecting our costs to continue to decline. I think preliminarily because we're ramping up Inner Mongolia Phase 5B, cost for Q2 is probably similar to slightly less than Q1. Then we think costs will continue to trend down for Q3 and Q4.
Alan Hon
Executive Director of Equity Research, JPMorgan
Well, I guess like one driver of the cost down would be the commencement of the new plant in Q2 that will be fully ramp up in Q3, right? Do you have like a target for the cost structure of the new plant?
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Okay. Right, I don't think we've discussed this earlier. You know, for the first time, Inner Mongolia cost is now below our Xinjiang cost, right? I don't know if you remember. The Inner Mongolia cost design was to be below Xinjiang but was higher than Xinjiang from Q3, Q4 until this quarter. Okay, also we had very significant improvements in quality as well. I think that gave us further confidence that once Inner Mongolia Phase 5B starts, it should be able to see similar or even better trajectory in terms of cost reduction and quality improvements, right? Because now we've done this once already, so we know where all the issues are.

Executive Director of Equity Research, JPMorgan
Got it. Thanks. These are all my questions.

Very great. Thank you, Alan.

Anita Zhu
Investor Relations, Daqo New Energy
Thank you. Hello, everyone. I'm Anita Zhu, the investor relations of Daqo New Energy. Thank you for joining our conference call today. Daqo New Energy just issued its financial results for Q4 and fiscal year 2023, which can be found on our website at www.dqsolar.com. Today, attending the conference call, we have our chairman and CEO, Mr. Xiang Xu, our CFO, Mr. Ming Yang, and myself. The call today will begin with an update from Mr. Xu on market conditions and company operations, and then Mr. Yang will discuss the company's financial performance for the quarter and the year.
After that, we'll open the floor to Q&A from the audience. Before we begin the formal remarks, I would like to remind you that certain statements on today's call, including expected future operational and financial performance, and industry growth, are forward-looking statements that are made under the safe harbor provisions of the US Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements involve inherent risks and uncertainties. A number of factors could cause actual results to differ materially from those contained in any forward-looking statements. Further information regarding these and other risks is included in the reports or documents we have filed with or furnished to the Securities and Exchange Commission. These statements only reflect our current and preliminary view as of today, and may be subject to change. Our ability to achieve these projections is subject to risks and uncertainties.
All information provided in today's call is as of today, and we undertake no duty to update such information except as required under applicable law. Also, during the call, we'll occasionally reference monetary amounts in US dollar terms. Please keep in mind that our functional currency is the Chinese RMB. We offer these translations into US dollars solely for the convenience of the audience. Mr. Xu will make his remarks regarding current market conditions and company performance in Chinese, which I will translate into English after he finishes. Now I'll turn the call to our CEO.
Xiang Xu
Chairman and CEO, Daqo New Energy
Thank you, Anita。 我是徐翔，大全新能源的CEO。感谢大家参加今天的电话会议。2023年是太阳能行业充满挑战与机遇的一年，全球装机量创下新纪录的同时，多晶硅市场价格却处于近期的历史低位。面对这样的环境，我们的团队展现出卓越的奉献精神和执行力。在2023年，我们成功实现19.7831万吨的年度多晶硅产量，达到了我们设定的19.6到19.9万吨的指导目标。产量与2022年的13.3812万吨相比，同比增长47.8%，销售量也达到了20万吨，较2022年的13.2909万吨增长了50%。全球太阳能光伏产品需求量在2023年强劲增长，但多晶硅市场价格却经历了剧烈的波动。2022年多晶硅因供应链上下游产能错配使得供不应求，价格持续处于高位的情况从2023年初得到缓解，多晶硅价格开始逐渐回落。因此，多晶硅的平均销售单价从2022年的每公斤$32.54大幅下降至2023年的每公斤$11.48。尽管平均单价的大幅下降导致我们的收入从2022年的$46亿减少至2023年的$23亿，但销售量的增加在一定程度上抵消了销售单价的下降。公司2023年的毛利率仍然表现强劲，达到了39.9%。公司在2023年内经营性现金流入约为$16亿，维持了健康的资产负债表，没有任何有息负债。到2023年底，公司的现金余额为$30亿，现金和应收票据余额合计为$32亿。在第四季度，我们的两段多晶硅基地持续优化运营，提升生产的能力，总产量达到6.1014万吨，较上一季度增加了3,350吨。在第四季度，我们高质量的N型多晶硅产品受到了客户的强烈需求，我们的产品库存也保持在非常低的水平，使我们在接近年底的淡季期间能够有效抵御下行风险。随着新产能的释放，高质量制造商与新进者之间的价格差异在第四季度愈发明显。尽管市场竞争激烈，但由于我们在成本和质量方面的持续领先，让我们仍然保持盈利能力，我们的单位生产成本逐季下降，2023年第四季度较于去年同期下降约$1.2每公斤。我们的N型硅料产品占比在12月已接近60%。整体来看，虽然市场条件具有挑战性，但我们在第四季度实现了$1.28亿的税收之后摊销前利润，并保持了可观的现金流。我们预计2024年一季度多晶硅总产量约为6万吨到6.2万吨。与2023年第四季度相比，我们计划内蒙古5B项目于二季度投产，因此我们预计2024年全年生产量将达到28万吨至30万吨，较2023年增长约40%至50%。明年，十周年的多晶硅生产经验、全面数字化战略以及高度集成的生产体系，我们将进一步优化运营效率，并提升N型硅料在产品组合中的比例。行业层面，从2023年四季度起，由于积极性的需求放缓和库存过剩导致的硅片价格下跌，多晶硅均价从9月份的每公斤约87元人民币，降至12月份的每公斤65元人民币。从需求侧看，10月起，基于库存过剩及硅片价格下跌，拉晶厂纷纷下调开工率。N型组件报价在10月首次突破了1元人民币每瓦。太阳能电池产品价格几乎逼近其成本线。从供给侧看，中国多晶硅量产产量在第四季度相继逐月增加，大部分产量的增长来自于二三梯队的增长，其中包含一些新进入者。然而，高质量制造商的有效产能增长却远低于预期，直接拉大了与二三线厂商之间的价格差距。12月底，N型和P型多晶硅价格从每公斤65到68元人民币，和每公斤55到62元人民币。进入2024年上半年，我们预计多晶硅价格将受到中国春季的积极影响而略有反弹，并在二季度处于稳定。随着下游厂商向N型升级的步伐加快，N型TOPCon产品相对于P型PERC产品的高价格溢价将推动市场加速向N型产品全面转型。我们预计，基于这一趋势，2024年N型市场的供给相对紧张，对于高精度N型多晶硅的需求将保持强劲。回看过去一年，2023年是可再生能源增长获得重大突破的一年，全球向可再生能源加速转型，其中中国太阳能光伏市场的持续繁荣起到关键性的作用。2023年光伏新增装机量达到216.88吉瓦，创下历史新高，同比增长148%。尤其在12月份，中国单月光伏新增装机量是53吉瓦，约占全年光伏新增装机量的四分之一。随着光伏发电成本的不断降低，光伏已成为极具竞争力的发电方式，预计将产生大量额外的绿色能源供应。2023年为逐步淘汰P型产品奠定了基础。因此，我们坚信2024年将迎来N型产品主导行业的新时代。我们乐观地认为，通过进一步提升公司高效N型硅料的产品，并借助数字化转型优化成本结构，我们将把握全球光伏产业持续增长所带来的长期市场机遇，构建我们企业的竞争核心。2023年，我们在两个多晶硅生产基地各收集超过200亿条运营数据。我们坚信，我们是业内拥有最大多晶硅生产数据库的企业之一。我们已经开始尝试使用人工智能技术，将这些数据应用于提高产品组合中N型硅料的比例，降低生产成本，通过识别各个制造流程之间的关系，最终预测、建模出最优生产模型的输入范围去参考。展望未来，随着我们收集更多的数据点，并充分利用人工智能正向分析，我们期望进一步降低成本，提高效率并提升生产能力。现在请Anita替我翻译一下。[Foreign Language]
Anita Zhu
Investor Relations, Daqo New Energy
Hello everyone, this is Anita.
I'll now translate our CEO Mr. Zhu's remarks. 2023 was a year of unforeseen developments and challenges in the solar industry with record installation volumes worldwide, but also record low prices at the end of the year. Thanks to the dedication and valuable contribution of our team, we reached an annual poly production volume of 197,831 metric tons in 2023, meeting our guidance of 196,000 to 199,000 metric tons, and representing a 47.8% year-over-year growth rate compared to 133,812 metric tons produced in 2022. We sold 200,002 metric tons, 50% higher than 132,909 metric tons in 2022.
Despite robust demand growth for solar PV products globally in 2023, the high poly prices driven by capacity mismatches between upstream and downstream players and the resulting supply shortages that we have seen in 2022 were alleviated by early 2023. As a result, poly ASP declined significantly for the year to $11 per kilogram from $32.54 per kilogram in 2022. Our revenue was $2.3 billion in 2023 compared to $4.6 billion in 2022 due to much lower ASPs.
The decline was partially offset by the higher sales volume. Despite the challenging market conditions, gross margins still came in strong at 39.9% for 2023. The company generated a very strong operating cash flow of approximately $1.6 billion for the year and continued to maintain a healthy balance sheet with no financial debt. By the end of the year, the company had a cash balance of $3 billion and a combined cash and bank notes receivable balance of $3.2 billion.
During Q4, continued optimization of operations and improvements in yields and throughput at our two poly facilities resulted in total production volume of 61,014 metric tons, an increase of 3,350 metric tons compared to the previous quarter. Q4 saw solid demand from customers for high quality N-type poly and as a result, our finished goods inventory was at a very low level, which would have allowed us to effectively hedge against downside risks during the off-season period close to the end of the year. In Q4, as new capacity was released, the price disparity became more apparent between high quality manufacturers and new entrants.
Despite severe market conditions due to the addition of poly supply, we continued to maintain our leadership in both cost and quality. Compared to the end of last year, our production costs trended down quarter over quarter, reducing by approximately $1.2 per kilogram from Q4 2022 compared to that in Q4 2023. During the month of December, our N-type product mix reached approximately 60%. Overall, we maintained profitability despite the challenging market conditions, generating $128 million in EBITDA for Q4 and maintained a strong cash flow.
We expect our Q1 2024 total poly production volume to be approximately 60,000 metric tons to 62,000 metric tons. Similar to that for our Q4 2023, as the company maintains full production. We plan to begin initial production at our new Inner Mongolia 5B+ facility in Q2 2024, and as such, we anticipate full year 2024 production volume to be approximately 280,000 metric tons to 300,000 metric tons.
Approximately 40% to 50% higher than in 2023. With more than a decade of experience in poly production, as well as a fully digitalized and integrated production system that optimizes operational efficiency, will further increase entire production in the product mix. Debriefing on the industry, poly prices in Q4 declined from approximately CNY 87 per Kilogram for mono-grade poly in September to approximately CNY 65 per Kg in December, primarily due to a seasonally lower demand. On the demand side, in October, the ingot segment reduced utilization rates due to accumulated inventory and lower wafer prices. In November, N-type module prices dropped below 1 CNY per watt for the first time, and solar cell manufacturers could hardly make a profit.
On the supply side, poly production volumes in China continued to increase on a month-over-month basis in Q4, and tier two and tier three manufacturers, including new entrants, contributed most of the growth in poly supply. However, leading high quality manufacturers produced less than anticipated, widening the price gap between high quality manufacturers and tier two companies. Near the end of December, N-type and P-type poly prices came in at around CNY 65 to 68 per kilogram and CNY 55 to 62 per kilogram, respectively. Going to Q1 2024, we expect poly prices to rebound slightly in Q1, seasonally affected by the Chinese New Year and then stabilize in Q2.
The market transition to N-type products has been accelerating as downstream producers continue to switch to N-type products, driven by the higher price premium for N-type for N-type TOPCon products over P-type PERC products. We expect this trend to continue throughout 2024, with strong demand for higher purity N-type poly in a market with tight supply. Overall, 2023 was an unprecedented year, marking a step change for renewable energy growth. The global acceleration in the transition to renewable energy was primarily driven by China's booming solar market, with new solar PV capacity reaching record high at 216.88 GW, a 148% year-over-year growth. This surge was particularly evident in December, when China added 53 GW, which is roughly a quarter of the entire year's additional capacity. Solar has become one of the most competitive forms of power generation.
The continuous cost reduction in solar PV products and the associated reduction in solar energy generation costs are expected to create substantial additional clean energy demand. With 2023 setting the stage for gradually phasing out P-type products, we believe that 2024 will mark the year when N-type products dominate the industry. We are optimistic that we'll capture the long-term benefits of the growing global solar PV product market and maintain our competitive advantage by enhancing our higher efficiency N-type technology and optimizing our cost structure through digital transformation. In 2023 alone, we collected more than 20 billion manufacturing process data points at each of our poly production facilities. We believe that we have one of the largest pools of collected and stored poly production data among our peers in China.
We have begun to apply AI to this vast amount of data to help increase the proportion of N-type in our product mix and reduce our production costs by identifying relationships across discrete processes and ultimately predicting the optimal inputs and parameters that will yield the best production results. We expect that as we collect more data and further leverage our AI-powered analytics to provide additional insights, we'll be able to further reduce costs, achieve higher efficiency, and increase productivity. Now I'll turn the call to our CFO, Mr. Ming Yang, who will discuss the company's financial performance for the quarter. Ming, please go ahead.
Ming Yang
CFO, Daqo New Energy
Thank you, Anita. Hello, everyone, this is Ming Yang, CFO of Daqo New Energy. We appreciate you joining our Earnings Conference Call today. I'll first go over the company's Q4 2023 financial performance, then follow with our full year 2023 financial results. Revenue for Q4 2023 were CNY 477 million, compared to CNY 484.8 million in Q3 2023 and CNY 864.3 million in Q4 2022. The decrease in revenue compared to Q3 2023 was primarily due to a decrease in sales volume, mitigated by an increase in ASP. As Mr.
Xu mentioned earlier, ASP for Q4 was $7.90 per kilogram, which was 3.8% above Q3 ASP of $7.68 per kilogram. Gross profit was $87.2 million, compared to $67.8 million in Q3 2023, $669 million in Q4 2022. Gross margin was 18.3%, compared to 14% in Q3 2023 and 77% in Q4 2022. The increase in gross margin compared to Q3 2023 was primarily due to higher average selling price and lower production costs.
Despite an 8% increase in silicon metal procurement costs in Q4 compared to Q3, we managed to reduce costs slightly due to improvements in utilization, as well as other improvements in manufacturing efficiency. SG&A expenses were CNY 39 million compared to CNY 89.7 million in Q3 2023 and CNY 44 million in Q4 2022. SG&A expenses during the fourth quarter includes CNY 19.6 million in non-cash share-based compensation expense related to the company's share incentive plan, compared to CNY 46.3 million in Q3 2023. R&D expenses were CNY 3.3 million, compared to CNY 2.8 million in Q3 2023, and CNY 2.7 million in Q4 2022. R&D expenses can vary from period to period and reflect R&D activities that take place during the quarter.
R&D activities for the quarter were primarily related to quality improvements and N-type product research. Foreign exchange loss was CNY 0.8 million, compared to a gain of CNY 3.1 million in Q3 2023, and is attributed to the volatility and fluctuation in the USD, the CNY exchange rate during the quarter. Income from operations was CNY 83.3 million, compared to CNY 22.5 million in Q3 2023, and CNY 623 million in Q4 2022. Operating margin was 17.5% compared to 4.6% in Q3 2023, and 72.1% in Q4 2022.
Net income attributable to Daqo New Energy shareholders was CNY 44.9 million, compared to a net loss of -CNY 6.3 million in Q3 2023, and net income of CNY 332.7 million in Q4 2022. Earnings per basic ADS was $0.64, compared to loss per basic ADS of $0.09 in the third quarter, and earnings per basic ADS of $4.26 in Q4 2022. Adjusted net income attributable to Daqo New Energy shareholders, which excludes non-cash share-based compensation costs, was CNY 66 million compared to CNY 44 million in Q3 2023, and CNY 363 million in Q4 2022.
Adjusted earnings per basic ADS was $0.94, compared to $0.59 in Q3 2023, and $4.65 in Q4 2022. EBITDA was CNY 128.2 million, compared to CNY 70 million in Q3 2023, and CNY 649 million in Q4 2022. EBITDA margin was 26.9%, compared to 14.5% in Q3 2023, and 75% in Q4 2022. Now I will go over the company's full year 2023 financial results. Revenue for 2023 was CNY 2.3 billion, compared to CNY 4.6 billion in 2022. The decrease was primarily due to lower polysilicon average selling prices and partially mitigated by higher sales volume.
Gross profit was CNY 920.7 million for 2023, compared to CNY 3.4 billion in 2022. Gross margin was 39.9% compared to 74% in 2022. The decrease in gross profit was primarily due to lower average selling price. SG&A expenses were CNY 213 million, compared to CNY 354 million in 2022. The decrease was primarily related to a reduction in non-cash share-based compensation costs related to the company's share incentive plan. R&D expenses in 2023 were CNY 10 million, compared to CNY 10 million in 2022. Income from operations was CNY 783.4 million, compared to CNY 3 billion in 2022. Operating margin was 33.9% compared to 66% in 2022.
Net interest income was $52.3 million compared to $14.5 million in 2022. The increase in interest income for 2023 was due to the company's higher cash balance at banks. Income tax expense was $174 million compared to $577 million in 2022. Net income attributable to Daqo New Energy shareholders for the full year of 2023 was $421 million, compared to $1.8 billion in 2022. Earnings per basic ADS were $5.64, compared to $24 in 2022. Non-GAAP adjusted net income attributable to Daqo New Energy shareholders was $554 million, compared to $2.1 billion in 2022.
Adjusted earnings per basic ADS were $7.42 in 2023, compared to $27.97 in 2022. EBITDA was $918.6 million, compared to $3.15 billion in 2022. EBITDA margin was 39.8% compared to 68.4% in 2022. Now on the company's financial condition. As of 31 December 2023, the company had $3 billion in cash equivalents, and restricted cash, compared to $3.28 billion as of 30 September 2023, and $3.5 billion as of 31 December 2022.
At the end of 2023, the bank note receivable balance was CNY 116 million, compared to CNY 275.8 million as of 30 September 2023, and CNY 1.13 billion as of 31 December 2022. Notes receivable represent bank notes with maturity within six months. Now on the company's cash flow. For the 12 months ended 31 December 2023, net cash provided by operating activities was CNY 1.61 billion, compared to CNY 2.46 billion in the same period of 2022. For the 12 months ending 31 December 2023, net cash used in investing activities was CNY 1.19 billion, compared to CNY 998 million in the same period of 2022.
Net cash used in investing activities in 2023 was primarily related to the company's capital expenditures on the company's Phase 5A and Phase 5B poly expansion projects in Baotou City, Inner Mongolia. For the 12 months ended 31 December 2023, net cash used in financing activities was CNY 795 million, compared to CNY 1.47 billion of net cash provided by financing activities in the same period of 2022. The net cash used in financing activities in 2023 was primarily related to CNY 486 million in share purchases and CNY 303 million in dividend payments made by the company's subsidiary, Xinjiang Daqo, to its minority shareholders on China's A-share market. That concludes our prepared remarks. We will now open the call to Q&A from the audience. Operator, please begin.
Operator
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. To ask a question, you may press star then one on your touchtone phone.
